what_its_for: Selenium sulfide is used to treat dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis (a skin condition that causes flaky, scaly patches on the scalp or skin), and a fungal skin infection called tinea versicolor (a condition that causes discolored patches on the skin). It works by slowing down the growth of the fungus and skin cells that cause these problems.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a shampoo or lotion that you apply to your skin or scalp. For dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp: Wet your hair, apply the shampoo to your scalp, lather well, leave it on for 2 to 3 minutes, then rinse thoroughly. Wash your hands after use. For tinea versicolor on the body: Apply the lotion or shampoo to the affected skin areas, leave it on for 10 minutes, then rinse off completely. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, nose, mouth, or genitals. If it gets in your eyes, rinse right away with plenty of water.
dosing: For dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis: Use the shampoo 2 times per week for the first 2 weeks. After that, use it once a week, once every 2 weeks, or as directed by your doctor. For tinea versicolor: Apply to affected areas once a day for 7 days, or as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions, as dosing can vary depending on the product strength (1% or 2.5%).
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store selenium sulfide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Do not use after the expiration date on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting selenium sulfide in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on your genitals. If contact occurs, rinse the area thoroughly with water. Do not use on broken, cut, or inflamed skin unless your doctor tells you it is okay. Avoid using this medicine more often than prescribed, as it will not work faster and may cause irritation. Do not use other scalp or skin products on the treated area unless your doctor approves. Avoid coloring, bleaching, or perming your hair within 48 hours of using this product, as it may cause discoloration. Remove jewelry, especially gold or silver items, before applying, as selenium sulfide can damage metal.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice any of the following: increased redness, itching, burning, or irritation of the skin or scalp; hair loss or changes in hair color or texture; skin rash or allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face or throat, difficulty breathing); no improvement after using the medicine as directed; oily or dry scalp that gets worse. Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you swallow any of this medicine by accident.
when_it_works: For dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, you may notice improvement within 2 to 4 weeks of regular use. For tinea versicolor, the infection may clear within a few weeks, but skin discoloration (light or dark patches) may take several months to fully fade even after the infection is gone. Continue using the medicine for as long as your doctor recommends, even if you start feeling better.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using selenium sulfide if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid applying it to the nipple area if you are breastfeeding. Children: Selenium sulfide is generally not recommended for children under 2 years of age. Always check with your child's doctor before use. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are usually needed, but check with your doctor if you have sensitive skin. People with skin conditions: Do not use on raw, blistered, or severely inflamed skin without first checking with your doctor.
